subject: Science
question: Light travels along which geometric path through a uniform, transparent medium (Rectilinear Propagation of Light)?
explanation: Rectilinear propagation: light travels along straight lines, causing the formation of sharp shadows and pinhole camera images.

subject: Science
question: What is the phenomenon of bouncing back of light rays from a polished, shiny, or reflective surface called?
explanation: Reflection is the change in direction and bouncing back of a light wavefront at an interface between two different media.

subject: Science
question: What are the characteristics of an image formed by a flat PLANE MIRROR?
options: Erect (upright), Virtual (cannot be obtained on a screen), Same size as the object, and Laterally Inverted
explanation: A plane mirror forms an erect, virtual image of identical size, located at the same distance behind the mirror as the object in front.

subject: Science
question: What optical phenomenon causes your right hand to appear as the left hand and your left hand to appear as the right hand in a mirror image?
explanation: Lateral inversion is the apparent sideways reversal of left and right in a planar reflection.

subject: Science
question: Why is the word 'AMBULANCE' written in reverse laterally inverted script ('ECNALUBMA') on emergency medical vehicles?
options: So that drivers of vehicles ahead can read the word correctly as 'AMBULANCE' in their rear-view mirrors and immediately give way
It is a foreign language spelling
To confuse pedestrians on the road
explanation: Pre-inverting the lettering ensures that when viewed through a driver's rear-view mirror, lateral inversion renders 'AMBULANCE' right-side up.

subject: Science
question: A spherical mirror whose reflecting surface is curved INWARDS (like the inside surface of a shining spoon) is called a:
explanation: A concave mirror has an inward-curving converging reflecting surface.

subject: Science
question: A spherical mirror whose reflecting surface is curved OUTWARDS (like the back outer surface of a shining spoon) is called a:
explanation: A convex mirror has an outward-bulging diverging reflecting surface.

subject: Science
question: An image that can be formed and projected onto a physical SCREEN is called a:
explanation: A real image is formed by the actual physical intersection of reflected/refracted light rays and can be captured on a screen.

subject: Science
question: An image that CANNOT be obtained or projected on a screen is called a:
explanation: A virtual image occurs where light rays only appear to diverge from a point behind the mirror/lens and cannot be captured on a screen.

subject: Science
question: A transparent optical lens that is THICKER in the middle than at the edges, converging parallel light rays to a focus, is called a:
explanation: A convex lens is thicker at its center and converges incident parallel light rays toward a real focal point.

subject: Science
question: A transparent optical lens that is THINNER in the middle than at the edges, diverging light rays outwards, is called a:
explanation: A concave lens is thinner at the center than at the periphery, causing parallel light rays to diverge.

subject: Science
question: White sunlight consists of how many distinct spectral colors that can be split by a glass prism (VIBGYOR)?
options: Seven Colors (Violet, Indigo, Blue, Green, Yellow, Orange, Red)
explanation: White light is a polychromatic mixture of seven constituent spectral wavelengths: Violet, Indigo, Blue, Green, Yellow, Orange, Red (VIBGYOR).

subject: Science
question: Which type of spherical mirror is used by Dentists to see an enlarged, magnified, and erect image of a patient's teeth?
options: Concave Mirror (held close to the teeth within its focal length)
explanation: When an object is placed between the pole and principal focus of a concave mirror, it produces an erect, magnified, virtual image.

subject: Science
question: Why are CONVEX MIRRORS universally installed as side REAR-VIEW MIRRORS in cars, buses, and motorcycles?
options: They always form erect, diminished images and provide a vastly WIDER FIELD OF VIEW, allowing drivers to see large traffic behind them
They magnify objects to look ten times closer
They absorb heat from the road
explanation: Convex mirrors curve outwards, producing upright, diminished virtual images that capture an expansive panoramic field of traffic.

subject: Science
question: What type of spherical mirror is used as reflectors in automobile Headlights, Searchlights, and Solar Furnaces to throw powerful parallel beams of light?
options: Concave Mirrors (with the light bulb placed at its principal focus)
explanation: Placing a lamp bulb at the focal point of a concave mirror produces a powerful, non-diverging parallel beam of reflected light.

subject: Science
question: What type of lens is used as a simple Handheld MAGNIFYING GLASS to read fine print or examine small insect parts?
options: A Convex Lens (held close to the object)
explanation: A convex lens produces a magnified, upright, virtual image when an object is held within its focal distance (acting as a simple microscope).

subject: Science
question: What type of image is ALWAYS formed by a CONCAVE LENS, regardless of how far or close the object is placed?
options: Virtual, Erect (upright), and DIMINISHED (smaller in size than the object)
explanation: A diverging concave lens always forms a virtual, erect, and diminished image located between the optical center and the principal focus.

subject: Science
question: What is the phenomenon of splitting white sunlight into its seven constituent spectral colors when passing through a triangular Glass Prism called?
explanation: Dispersion occurs because different wavelengths (colors) of light refract (bend) at slightly different angles when passing through glass.

subject: Science
question: How is a natural RAINBOW formed in the sky after rain showers?
options: Millions of tiny suspended airborne raindrops act like miniature optical prisms, refracting, dispersing, and internally reflecting sunlight into a spectrum
Clouds paint colors in the sky with water
Sunlight reflects off ocean waves into the sky
explanation: Atmospheric raindrops act as spherical prisms: refracting light on entry, internally reflecting it, and dispersing it upon exit into an arc.

subject: Science
question: What happens when a circular circular disc painted with all seven rainbow color segments (Newton's Disc) is rotated RAPIDLY on its central axis?
options: The seven colors blend together due to the persistence of vision, and the disc appears completely WHITE (or pale grayish-white)
The disc becomes transparent like glass
explanation: Newton's disc demonstrates additive color synthesis: rapid retinal persistence of vision (~1/16 s) superimposes the 7 colors into white light.

subject: Science
question: If an object is placed at a distance of 0.5 m in front of a flat plane mirror, what is the total distance between the OBJECT and its IMAGE?
options: 1.0 m (0.5 m in front + 0.5 m behind = 1.0 m)
explanation: Image distance behind mirror equals object distance in front (d = 0.5 m). Total distance between object and image = 0.5 + 0.5 = 1.0 m.

subject: Science
question: David is observing his image in a plane mirror. The distance between the mirror and his image is 4 m. If he moves 1 m towards the mirror, what will be the new distance between David and his image?
options: 6 m (New object distance = 3 m ; New image distance = 3 m ; Total = 3 + 3 = 6 m)
explanation: When David moves 1 m closer, object distance = 4 - 1 = 3 m. Image distance = 3 m. Distance between David and his image = 3 + 3 = 6 m.

subject: Science
question: What happens when you focus direct bright sunlight onto a dry sheet of paper using a powerful CONVEX LENS for a couple of minutes?
options: The lens converges all solar rays to a single intense focal point; thermal concentration heats the paper until it scorches, smokes, and catches fire
The paper turns into a mirror
explanation: A converging convex lens focuses incident solar irradiance into a tiny focal spot, concentrating thermal energy above the paper's kindling point.

subject: Science
question: Why does the rear-view mirror of a car carry the printed safety warning: 'OBJECTS IN MIRROR ARE CLOSER THAN THEY APPEAR'?
options: Because convex mirrors form diminished (smaller) images, which makes approaching vehicles appear further away than their actual physical distance
Because the mirror has a magnifier
Because the glass is curved inwards
Because the mirror works with radio waves
explanation: Convex mirrors minify images to gain field-of-view; human visual perception equates smaller retinal size with greater distance.

subject: Science
question: Which color of light bends (refracts) the MOST and which color bends the LEAST when white light passes through a glass prism?
options: VIOLET bends the most (shortest wavelength), and RED bends the least (longest wavelength)
Red bends the most, and Violet bends the least
Green bends the most, and Yellow bends the least
All colors bend at the exact same angle
explanation: Cauchy's dispersion formula: refractive index is inversely proportional to wavelength. High-frequency violet refracts most; low-frequency red refracts least.

subject: Science
question: What type of mirror is used in large Solar Cookers to concentrate solar energy onto cooking pots?
explanation: Large parabolic concave mirrors concentrate solar irradiance onto the focal point where cooking utensils are placed.

subject: Science
question: Which of the following optical instruments uses combinations of CONVEX LENSES to magnify distant celestial objects like the Moon and planets?
explanation: Refracting astronomical telescopes combine an objective convex lens of long focal length with an ocular eyepiece convex lens to resolve distant stars.

subject: Science
question: What is the speed of light in vacuum (c)?
explanation: The universal speed of light in vacuum is approximately 299,792,458 m/s (≈ 3 × 10⁸ m/s or 300,000 km/s).

subject: Science
question: Sir Isaac Newton proved in 1666 that white light is a combination of colors by using two identical glass prisms. How did he conduct this experiment?
options: He placed a second identical inverted glass prism in the path of the dispersed spectrum from the first prism, recombining all seven colors back into a single beam of WHITE LIGHT
He painted the second prism with oil
He melted the second prism into water
He burned the light beam with a match
explanation: Newton's classic recombination experiment: an inverted second prism cancels the angular dispersion of the first prism, synthesizing white light.

subject: Science
question: Why does a pencil partly immersed in a glass tumbler of water appear BENT or BROKEN at the water-air boundary?
options: Due to Refraction: light rays emerging from the underwater portion of the pencil bend away from the normal as they pass from denser water into rarer air
Because water acts as a mirror
explanation: Refraction at the planar water-air boundary shifts the apparent position of the submerged pencil tip upwards, creating an apparent bend.

subject: Science
question: How does a Periscope (used in submarines and military trenches) enable an observer to see objects over walls or above the water surface?
options: It uses TWO parallel plane mirrors inclined at an angle of 45° to each other, successively reflecting light rays downwards through a tube
It uses an electric camera with a screen
It uses two magnifying lenses only
explanation: A periscope utilizes two plane mirrors set at 45° to provide twin successive 90° reflections, shifting the line of sight over obstacles.

explanation: A cinema projector creates a real inverted image on a screen. Scenarios 1 (close), 2, and 3 produce virtual images.

subject: Science
question: Why does the primary rainbow always appear in the sky in the direction OPPOSITE to the position of the Sun (e.g. in the East in the late afternoon)?
options: Because sunlight must enter the raindrops from behind the observer and be internally reflected back towards the observer's eyes at an angle of ~42°
Because the Moon pulls the rainbow
Because clouds only exist in the east
Because wind blows the colors opposite to the sun
explanation: Rainbow geometry requires anti-solar alignment: the observer's back is to the sun so that internal reflection at ~40–42° enters the retina.

subject: Science
question: What is the optical mechanism of 'Persistence of Vision' in human eye biology that makes motion pictures and Newton's rotating color disc work?
options: The visual impression of an image on the human retina remains for approximately 1/16th of a second after the light stimulus disappears, allowing sequential frames to blend seamlessly into continuous motion or white light
The eye stores images in memory for one hour
The cornea turns into a prism
explanation: Retinal photoreceptors retain photochemical activation for ~1/16 s (persistence of vision), enabling cinematic animation and color fusion.

subject: Science
question: Why are high-intensity parabolic Concave Mirrors used in solar thermal power plants (like Ivanpah or Bhadla Solar Park)?
options: Thousands of giant concave mirrors (heliostats) track the Sun and concentrate thousands of megawatts of thermal solar flux onto a central molten-salt receiver tower to generate superheated steam for turbines
To produce cold water for cities
To reflect light away from the Earth
explanation: Concentrated Solar Power (CSP) employs massive concave parabolic mirror fields to focus solar flux onto molten-salt heat exchangers.

options: Light—the primary medium of visual perception—governs rectilinear ray propagation, geometric reflection, refractive dispersion, and spherical image formation that underpins modern microscopy, vision correction, astronomical exploration, and solar energy technologies
That light has no physical laws
That colors exist only inside glass prisms
That mirrors can only be made of silver
explanation: Chapter 11 establishes foundational geometric optics: rectilinear ray propagation, planar and spherical reflection/refraction, and chromatic dispersion.

A market trading only livestock animals

A royal family's personal bank account

chapter: Chapter 11: Inside Our Earth, Rocks, Minerals & Dynamic Landforms
question: The continuous geological transformation of one rock type into another under cyclical physical processes is known as the:
explanation: The rock cycle describes the cyclic transitions among igneous, sedimentary, and metamorphic rocks driven by geological forces.

subject: Social Science
chapter: Chapter 11: Inside Our Earth, Rocks, Minerals & Dynamic Landforms
question: Which white metamorphic rock, transformed from sedimentary limestone under high temperature, was used to construct the world-famous TAJ MAHAL at Agra?
explanation: Makrana white marble (metamorphosed limestone from Rajasthan) was used to construct the iconic Taj Mahal.

subject: Social Science
chapter: Chapter 11: Inside Our Earth, Rocks, Minerals & Dynamic Landforms
question: What is the fundamental difference between ENDOGENIC forces and EXOGENIC forces shaping the Earth's surface?
options: Endogenic forces originate deep within the Earth's interior (causing earthquakes, volcanic eruptions, and mountain building) ; Exogenic forces operate on the Earth's exterior surface (weathering and erosion by rivers, wind, glaciers, sea waves)
Endogenic forces are in oceans and Exogenic forces are in air
Endogenic forces cause rain and Exogenic forces cause fire
explanation: Endogenic = internal tectonic/magmatic forces; Exogenic = external geomorphic weathering and erosional agents.

subject: Social Science
chapter: Chapter 11: Inside Our Earth, Rocks, Minerals & Dynamic Landforms
question: What is the place in the Earth's crust where an earthquake vibration originates called, and what is the point on the surface directly above it called?
options: The origin point inside the crust is the FOCUS (Hypocenter) ; The point on the surface directly above the focus is the EPICENTER
Surface is Focus and interior is Epicenter
explanation: The focus is the subterranean seismic rupture origin; the epicenter is the surface point directly perpendicular above the focus.

subject: Social Science
chapter: Chapter 11: Inside Our Earth, Rocks, Minerals & Dynamic Landforms
question: Which scientific instrument is used to record and measure the vibrations and waves of an Earthquake?
options: A Seismograph (and measured on the Richter Scale)
explanation: Earthquake seismic tremors are recorded by seismographs, with magnitude quantified on the logarithmic Richter scale.

subject: Social Science
chapter: Chapter 11: Inside Our Earth, Rocks, Minerals & Dynamic Landforms
question: What are the large S-shaped curves and loops formed by a meandering river across a flat valley plain called?
explanation: Meanders are sinuous serpentine curves formed along a mature river's course by continuous lateral erosion and deposition.

subject: Social Science
chapter: Chapter 11: Inside Our Earth, Rocks, Minerals & Dynamic Landforms
question: What happens when a river meander loop becomes so acute that the river cuts through the narrow neck, leaving behind a crescent-shaped cutoff water body?
explanation: An oxbow lake is a crescent-shaped cutoff lake formed when a river cuts straight through a meandering loop neck during floods.

subject: Social Science
chapter: Chapter 11: Inside Our Earth, Rocks, Minerals & Dynamic Landforms
question: What is the triangular landform formed at the mouth of a river where it enters the sea and deposits its entire sediment load called?
options: A River Delta (like the Sundarbans Delta)
explanation: A delta is a triangular depositional landform formed at a river mouth by distributaries depositing silt into a standing sea/lake.

subject: Social Science
chapter: Chapter 11: Inside Our Earth, Rocks, Minerals & Dynamic Landforms
question: What are the isolated rock pillars left standing in the ocean after the roofs of 'Sea Arches' collapse under relentless wave erosion called?
explanation: Coastal wave progression: sea cave → sea arch (roof pierced) → sea stack (roof collapses, leaving isolated vertical rock pillars).

subject: Social Science
chapter: Chapter 11: Inside Our Earth, Rocks, Minerals & Dynamic Landforms
question: What are the rock formations in hot deserts that have a narrow base and a wide top due to wind eroding the lower section faster than the upper part called?
explanation: Mushroom rocks develop in arid deserts because wind-borne sand abrasion is concentrated within 1 meter of the ground, undercutting rock bases.

subject: Social Science
chapter: Chapter 11: Inside Our Earth, Rocks, Minerals & Dynamic Landforms
question: What are the crescent-shaped or ridge-like mounds of sand deposited by desert winds called?
explanation: Sand dunes are dynamic depositional mounds of sand accumulated by aeolian wind action in desert landscapes.

subject: Social Science
chapter: Chapter 11: Inside Our Earth, Rocks, Minerals & Dynamic Landforms
question: What are the vast deposits of fine, yellowish, wind-blown silt found extensively in northern China called?
explanation: Loess is fine, mineral-rich, windblown silt deposited over extensive regional plains (notably in China's Loess Plateau).

subject: Social Science
chapter: Chapter 11: Inside Our Earth, Rocks, Minerals & Dynamic Landforms
question: What are the ridges of rocks, gravel, sand, and clay deposited by melting glaciers along their valley margins called?
explanation: Glacial moraines are linear ridges of unsorted glacial till (boulders, gravel, sand, clay) dumped by retreating valley glaciers.

subject: Social Science
chapter: Chapter 11: Inside Our Earth, Rocks, Minerals & Dynamic Landforms
question: Which of the following sedimentary rocks was extensively used to construct the historic RED FORT in Delhi?
explanation: The Mughal Red Fort in Delhi and Agra Fort were constructed using red quartzitic sandstone quarried in Rajasthan.

subject: Social Science
chapter: Chapter 11: Inside Our Earth, Rocks, Minerals & Dynamic Landforms
question: What are 'Fossils' found embedded within sedimentary rock strata?
options: The preserved mineralized remains, impressions, or traces of ancient dead plants, animals, and microorganisms trapped in layered rocks millions of years ago
explanation: Fossils are organic paleontological relics entombed within sedimentary depositional beds over geological epochs.

subject: Social Science
chapter: Chapter 11: Inside Our Earth, Rocks, Minerals & Dynamic Landforms
question: What is the 'Asthenosphere' in geology?
options: The semi-fluid, ductile upper region of the Earth's mantle directly below the lithosphere where extreme heat permits solid rock to flow slowly, driving plate tectonics
The layer of air around the Earth
The solid center of the core
explanation: The ductile asthenosphere undergoes slow convection currents, transporting the rigid lithospheric tectonic plates floating above it.

subject: Social Science
chapter: Chapter 11: Inside Our Earth, Rocks, Minerals & Dynamic Landforms
question: Why is the inner core of the Earth solid despite scorching temperatures exceeding 5,000°C?
options: The colossal, overwhelming overlying gravitational Pressure at the Earth's center compresses the iron-nickel atoms into a solid crystalline state
Because the core is made of ice
Because no heat reaches the center
Because the core rotates too fast
explanation: Extreme lithostatic pressure (~3.6 million atmospheres) raises the melting point of iron-nickel, keeping the inner core solid.

subject: Social Science
chapter: Chapter 11: Inside Our Earth, Rocks, Minerals & Dynamic Landforms
question: What is the steep, nearly vertical rock face rising directly above sea water formed by continuous wave erosion called?
explanation: A sea cliff is a dramatic vertical coastal rock precipice produced by hydraulic wave action undercutting the shoreface.

subject: Social Science
chapter: Chapter 11: Inside Our Earth, Rocks, Minerals & Dynamic Landforms
question:
Read the statements:
Assertion (A): The Earth's crust is fragmented into multiple rigid Lithospheric Plates that move continuously by a few millimeters each year.
Reason (R): Slow thermal convection currents in the molten and ductile magma within the mantle drive the perpetual continental drift, seafloor spreading, and plate collisions.
Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A).
explanation: Plate tectonics is driven by mantle thermal convection cells carrying tectonic lithospheric slabs across the asthenosphere.

subject: Social Science
chapter: Chapter 11: Inside Our Earth, Rocks, Minerals & Dynamic Landforms
question:
Spot the IMPOSTER in the following rock types and their metamorphic transformations:
Group:
1. Limestone -> Marble
2. Clay / Shale -> Slate
3. Granite -> Gneiss
4. Liquid Water -> Igneous Basalt
options: Transformation 4 (Basalt is formed by the cooling of molten LAVA/MAGMA, NOT by freezing liquid water)
explanation: Transformation 4 is an absurd impossibility: basalt is an extrusive igneous rock crystallized from silicate lava melts.

subject: Social Science
chapter: Chapter 11: Inside Our Earth, Rocks, Minerals & Dynamic Landforms
question:
Analyze the three types of seismic earthquake waves generated during a tectonic fault slip:
1. P-Waves (Primary / Longitudinal waves - fastest, travel through solid, liquid, and gas)
2. S-Waves (Secondary / Transverse waves - travel ONLY through solids)
3. L-Waves (Surface waves - slowest, cause maximum destructive ground displacement)
How did the behavior of S-Waves reveal the nature of the Earth's OUTER CORE?
options: S-Waves completely disappear at the core-mantle boundary (2,900 km depth), proving conclusively that the Earth's OUTER CORE is in a MOLTEN LIQUID state
S-Waves prove that the whole Earth is hollow
S-Waves show that the core is made of diamond
explanation: The S-wave shadow zone beyond 105° proved that the outer core cannot support shear stress, establishing its liquid metallic nature.

subject: Social Science
chapter: Chapter 11: Inside Our Earth, Rocks, Minerals & Dynamic Landforms
question:
Match Column I (Geomorphic Landforms) with Column II (Primary Natural Agents of Erosion / Deposition):
(a) Meanders and Oxbow Lakes -> (i) Running River Water (Fluvial agent)
(b) Mushroom Rocks and Dunes   -> (ii) Desert Wind Action (Aeolian agent)
(c) Moraines and U-Valleys    -> (iii) Moving Glacial Ice (Glacial agent)
(d) Sea Stacks and Sea Arches -> (iv) Coastal Ocean Waves (Marine agent)
explanation: Meanders = rivers; Mushroom rocks = wind; Moraines = glaciers; Stacks = sea waves.

subject: Social Science
chapter: Chapter 11: Inside Our Earth, Rocks, Minerals & Dynamic Landforms
question:
Read the statements regarding the Earth's geological layers:
Statement 1: The crust forms only 1% of the volume of the Earth, the mantle forms 84%, and the core forms 15%.
Statement 2: The radius of the Earth is approximately 6,371 km.
Statement 3: The Earth's mantle is made of liquid gold and silver.
Which statements are TRUE?
explanation: Statement 3 is an absurd falsehood (mantle is solid silicate rock). Statements 1 (volumetric ratios) and 2 (Earth radius = 6,371 km) are accurate.

subject: Social Science
chapter: Chapter 11: Inside Our Earth, Rocks, Minerals & Dynamic Landforms
question: How did the massive volcanic lava plateaus (like the DECCAN TRAPS in western and central India) form around 66 million years ago?
options: Enormous fissure eruptions poured millions of cubic kilometers of fluid basaltic magma over the landscape, creating thick horizontal flood-basalt lava sheets
A giant meteor made of basalt crashed into India
Basalt was washed down from the Himalayas by rivers
Humans mined and piled up the basalt rocks
explanation: The Deccan Traps formed via flood basalt volcanism during India's passage over the Reunion thermal mantle plume in the Late Cretaceous.

subject: Social Science
chapter: Chapter 11: Inside Our Earth, Rocks, Minerals & Dynamic Landforms
question: What is the crucial role of the Earth's molten metallic liquid OUTER CORE in generating the GEOMAGNETIC FIELD (the Geodynamo)?
options: Thermal convection currents of molten iron and nickel, combined with planetary Coriolis rotation, generate powerful electric currents that produce the Earth's protective magnetic shield against solar radiation
It acts as a giant refrigerator cooling the crust
It creates oxygen for the atmosphere
explanation: The convective geodynamo in the liquid iron outer core generates Earth's magnetosphere, shielding life from lethal solar winds.

subject: Social Science
chapter: Chapter 11: Inside Our Earth, Rocks, Minerals & Dynamic Landforms
question:
Consider four geographical features:
1. The Grand Canyon (USA)
2. The Sundarbans Mangrove Delta (India/Bangladesh)
3. The Victoria Falls (Zambia/Zimbabwe)
4. Barchan sand dunes of Thar Desert (Rajasthan)
Which of these are purely FLUVIAL landforms formed by running river water?
explanation: Canyon (river erosion), Delta (river deposition), Waterfall (river knickpoint) are fluvial. Barchan dunes are aeolian wind landforms.

subject: Social Science
chapter: Chapter 11: Inside Our Earth, Rocks, Minerals & Dynamic Landforms
question: What is the geological origin of 'Natural Levees' along the banks of mature lowland rivers?
options: During seasonal overbank flooding, coarse sediments are deposited immediately along river margins where water velocity drops first, building elevated natural embankment ridges
Wind blew sand onto the river banks
explanation: Natural levees are coarse sediment embankments deposited parallel to river channels during flood overflows.

subject: Social Science
chapter: Chapter 11: Inside Our Earth, Rocks, Minerals & Dynamic Landforms
question: Why do metamorphic rocks often exhibit distinct parallel mineral bands, foliation, or striped textures (such as in Gneiss or Schist)?
options: Extreme directional tectonic pressure and shear stress force platy and elongated minerals to realign perpendicular to the compressive stress axis
Because different colored paints were applied to them
Because water carved lines into them
Because they were made by lightning
explanation: Metamorphic foliation is the structural alignment of mineral grains perpendicular to principal tectonic stress directions under high P-T conditions.

subject: Social Science
chapter: Chapter 11: Inside Our Earth, Rocks, Minerals & Dynamic Landforms
question: What distinguishes a 'Mineral' from an ordinary rock?
options: A mineral is a naturally occurring inorganic substance with a definite chemical composition and an ordered internal atomic crystalline structure, whereas a rock is an aggregate of one or more minerals
Minerals do not exist inside rocks
explanation: Minerals are homogeneous crystalline chemical compounds (e.g. Quartz, Feldspar, Calcite), whereas rocks are heterogeneous lithified aggregates.

subject: Social Science
chapter: Chapter 11: Inside Our Earth, Rocks, Minerals & Dynamic Landforms
question: What master geographical insight is established in Chapter 11 of NCERT Class 7 Geography?
options: The Earth is a dynamic, living planet in perpetual transformation—where internal convective forces constantly build and reshape lithospheric crust, while external erosional agents continuously sculpt majestic landforms that sustain human agriculture, civilizational settlements, and mineral wealth
That the Earth's surface never changes
That rocks have no economic or ecological value
That all continents will sink into the core tomorrow
explanation: Chapter 11 establishes dynamic planetary geomorphology: the perpetual equilibrium between endogenic tectonic construction and exogenic denudational sculpting.

subject: Hindi Grammar
question: जिन शब्दों के रूप में लिंग, वचन, कारक, काल आदि के प्रभाव से कभी कोई विकार (परिवर्तन) नहीं होता, उन्हें क्या कहते हैं?
explanation: अव्यय (अविकारी): जिनका रूप कभी नहीं बदलता (जैसे: और, किन्तु, धीरे-धीरे, प्रतिदिन, अरे, तक)।

subject: Hindi Grammar
question: हिंदी व्याकरण में अव्यय के मुख्य रूप से कितने भेद माने जाते हैं?
options: 5 भेद (1. क्रियाविशेषण, 2. संबंधबोधक, 3. समुच्चयबोधक, 4. विस्मयादिबोधक, 5. निपात)
explanation: अव्यय के 5 भेद हैं: क्रियाविशेषण, संबंधबोधक, समुच्चयबोधक, विस्मयादिबोधक और निपात।

subject: Hindi Grammar
question: क्रिया की विशेषता (समय, स्थान, परिमाण, रीति आदि) बताने वाले अव्यय शब्दों को क्या कहते हैं?
explanation: क्रियाविशेषण: जो अव्यय शब्द क्रिया के घटित होने की विशेषता (कब, कहाँ, कैसे, कितना) बताते हैं।

subject: Hindi Grammar
question: क्रियाविशेषण के मुख्य रूप से कितने भेद होते हैं?
explanation: क्रियाविशेषण के 4 भेद हैं: कालवाचक (कब), स्थानवाचक (कहाँ), परिमाणवाचक (कितना), रीतिवाचक (कैसे)।

subject: Hindi Grammar
question: 'कछुआ धीरे-धीरे चलता है।' वाक्य में 'धीरे-धीरे' किस प्रकार का क्रियाविशेषण है?
options: रीतिवाचक क्रियाविशेषण (Adverb of Manner - कैसे चलता है)
explanation: 'धीरे-धीरे' क्रिया के संपन्न होने की रीति (ढंग) बता रहा है, अतः यह रीतिवाचक क्रियाविशेषण है।

subject: Hindi Grammar
question: 'हम प्रतिदिन व्यायाम करते हैं।' वाक्य में 'प्रतिदिन' किस प्रकार का क्रियाविशेषण है?
options: कालवाचक क्रियाविशेषण (Adverb of Time - कब करते हैं)
explanation: 'प्रतिदिन' क्रिया के होने का समय (काल) बता रहा है, अतः यह कालवाचक क्रियाविशेषण है।

subject: Hindi Grammar
question: 'बच्चे ऊपर खेल रहे हैं।' वाक्य में 'ऊपर' किस प्रकार का क्रियाविशेषण है?
options: स्थानवाचक क्रियाविशेषण (Adverb of Place - कहाँ खेल रहे हैं)
explanation: 'ऊपर' क्रिया के संपन्न होने का स्थान बता रहा है, अतः यह स्थानवाचक क्रियाविशेषण है।

subject: Hindi Grammar
question: 'कम बोलो, अधिक काम करो।' वाक्य में 'कम' और 'अधिक' किस प्रकार के क्रियाविशेषण हैं?
explanation: 'कम' और 'अधिक' क्रिया की मात्रा/परिमाण का बोध कराते हैं, अतः परिमाणवाचक क्रियाविशेषण हैं।

subject: Hindi Grammar
question: जो अव्यय शब्द संज्ञा या सर्वनाम के बाद आकर उसका संबंध वाक्य के अन्य शब्दों से जोड़ते हैं (जैसे: 'के बिना', 'के साथ', 'के सामने'), वे क्या कहलाते हैं?
explanation: संबंधबोधक: संज्ञा/सर्वनाम के पीछे प्रयुक्त होकर वाक्य के अन्य पदों से संबंध बताने वाले अव्यय।

subject: Hindi Grammar
question: दो शब्दों, वाक्यांशों या वाक्यों को आपस में जोड़ने वाले अव्यय शब्दों (जैसे: 'और', 'किन्तु', 'परन्तु', 'क्योंकि') को क्या कहते हैं?
explanation: समुच्चयबोधक (योजक): दो पदों, उपवाक्यों या वाक्यों को परस्पर जोड़ने वाले अव्यय शब्द।

subject: Hindi Grammar
question: हर्ष, शोक, भय, आश्चर्य, घृणा, चेतावनी आदि तीव्र मनोभावों को प्रकट करने वाले अव्यय (जैसे: 'अरे!', 'वाह!', 'शाबाश!', 'हाय!') क्या कहलाते हैं?
explanation: विस्मयादिबोधक: मनोभावों (आश्चर्य, दुःख, उल्लास) को व्यक्त करने वाले अव्यय, जिनके बाद '!' चिह्न लगता है।

subject: Hindi Grammar
question: जो अव्यय शब्द किसी शब्द के बाद लगकर उसके अर्थ में विशेष 'बल' (Emphasis) प्रदान करते हैं (जैसे: 'ही', 'भी', 'तो', 'मात्र', 'तक'), वे क्या कहलाते हैं?
explanation: निपात: किसी पद पर विशेष बल देने के लिए प्रयुक्त होने वाले अव्यय (जैसे: 'वह भी जाएगा', 'तुम ही आओगे')।

subject: Hindi Grammar
question: क्रियाविशेषण और विशेषण में क्या मूलभूत व्याकरणिक अंतर होता है?
options: विशेषण 'संज्ञा या सर्वनाम' की विशेषता बताता है (जैसे: 'मीठा सेब') ; जबकि क्रियाविशेषण 'क्रिया' की विशेषता बताता है (जैसे: 'मधुर गाता है')
दोनों में कोई अंतर नहीं होता
विशेषण केवल वाक्यों के अंत में आता है
explanation: विशेषण संज्ञा/सर्वनाम की विशेषता प्रकट करता है; क्रियाविशेषण क्रिया की विशेषता (ढंग/समय/स्थान/मात्रा) बताता है।

subject: Hindi Grammar
question: समुच्चयबोधक (योजक) के मुख्य रूप से दो भेद कौन-से होते हैं?
options: 1. समानाधिकरण समुच्चयबोधक (और, तथा, या, किन्तु, परन्तु, इसलिए) ; 2. व्यधिकरण समुच्चयबोधक (क्योंकि, ताकि, यद्यपि-तथापि, जिससे कि)
explanation: समुच्चयबोधक के 2 भेद हैं: समानाधिकरण (समान स्तर के उपवाक्यों को जोड़ने वाले) और व्यधिकरण (आश्रित उपवाक्य जोड़ने वाले)।

subject: Hindi Grammar
question: 'विद्या के बिना जीवन व्यर्थ है।' इस वाक्य में 'के बिना' किस प्रकार का अव्यय है?
explanation: 'के बिना' संज्ञा 'विद्या' के बाद आकर वाक्य के अन्य शब्दों से संबंध जोड़ रहा है, अतः यह संबंधबोधक अव्यय है।

subject: Hindi Grammar
question: 'वह विद्यालय नहीं गया क्योंकि वह बीमार था।' इस वाक्य में 'क्योंकि' किस प्रकार का समुच्चयबोधक है?
explanation: 'क्योंकि' मुख्य उपवाक्य के साथ कारण बताने वाले आश्रित उपवाक्य को जोड़ता है, अतः यह कारणवाचक व्यधिकरण समुच्चयबोधक है।

subject: Hindi Grammar
question: 'शाबाश! तुमने परीक्षा में प्रथम स्थान प्राप्त किया।' वाक्य में 'शाबाश!' किस मनोभाव को प्रकट करने वाला विस्मयादिबोधक है?
explanation: 'शाबाश!' प्रशंसा, उत्साह और अनुमोदन व्यक्त करने वाला विस्मयादिबोधक अव्यय है।

subject: Hindi Grammar
question: 'राम ने ही यह काम किया है।' और 'राम ने यह काम भी किया है।' में 'ही' और 'भी' निपात का क्या प्रभाव है?
options: 'ही' केवल राम पर अनन्य बल देता है (किसी अन्य ने नहीं) ; जबकि 'भी' अतिरिक्तता/समावेश का बोध कराता है (अन्य के साथ राम ने भी)
दोनों वाक्यों का अर्थ बिल्कुल एकसमान है
निपात से वाक्य में कोई परिवर्तन नहीं होता
explanation: 'ही' सीमा/अवधारण (केवल वही) तथा 'भी' समुच्चय/समावेश (वह भी) का विशिष्ट अर्थगत बल प्रदान करता है।

subject: Hindi Grammar
question:
'भीतर' शब्द का प्रयोग निम्नलिखित दो वाक्यों में किस रूप में हुआ है?
वाक्य 1: 'वह भीतर गया।'
वाक्य 2: 'वह कमरे के भीतर गया।'
क्रमशः सही भेद पहचानिए:
options: वाक्य 1 में 'भीतर' = स्थानवाचक क्रियाविशेषण ; वाक्य 2 में 'के भीतर' = संबंधबोधक अव्यय
वाक्य 1 में संबंधबोधक और वाक्य 2 में क्रियाविशेषण है
explanation: अकेले क्रिया की विशेषता बताने पर क्रियाविशेषण ('भीतर गया'), संज्ञा के साथ परसर्गयुक्त संबंध जोड़ने पर संबंधबोधक ('कमरे के भीतर')।

subject: Hindi Grammar
question: 'छी-छी! यहाँ कितनी गंदगी फैली है।' वाक्य में 'छी-छी!' किस प्रकार का विस्मयादिबोधक है?
explanation: 'छी-छी!' घृणा, अरुचि और तिरस्कार का मनोभाव प्रकट करता है।

subject: Hindi Grammar
question: 'तुम चाय पियोगे अथवा कॉफ़ी?' वाक्य में 'अथवा' किस प्रकार का समुच्चयबोधक है?
explanation: 'अथवा / या' दो विकल्पों में से किसी एक के चयन का बोध कराने वाला विभाजक समुच्चयबोधक है।

subject: Hindi Grammar
question: 'उसने बहुत परिश्रम किया किन्तु सफल न हो सका।' वाक्य में 'किन्तु' किस प्रकार का समुच्चयबोधक है?
explanation: 'किन्तु / परन्तु / लेकिन' पहले उपवाक्य के विपरीत परिणाम/विरोध को प्रकट करता है।

subject: Hindi Grammar
question: 'परिश्रम करो ताकि परीक्षा में सफल हो सको।' वाक्य में 'ताकि' किस प्रकार का समुच्चयबोधक है?
explanation: 'ताकि / जिससे कि' कार्य के उद्देश्य (प्रयोजन) को स्पष्ट करने वाला उद्देश्यवाचक व्यधिकरण समुच्चयबोधक है।

subject: Hindi Grammar
question: 'अरे! तुम कब आए?' वाक्य में 'अरे!' किस भाव को व्यक्त करता है?
explanation: 'अरे!' आकस्मिक विस्मय और आश्चर्य प्रकट करने वाला अव्यय है।

subject: Hindi Grammar
question: 'घर के सामने एक विशाल बरगद का पेड़ है।' वाक्य में 'के सामने' क्या है?
explanation: 'के सामने' संज्ञा 'घर' और 'बरगद के पेड़' के बीच स्थानिक संबंध स्थापित करने वाला संबंधबोधक अव्यय है।

subject: Hindi Grammar
question: 'वह दिनभर पढ़ता रहा।' वाक्य में 'दिनभर' में 'भर' क्या है?
explanation: 'भर' (जैसे: रातभर, दिनभर) व्याप्ति और सीमा पर बल देने वाला निपात है।

subject: Hindi Grammar
question: 'अचानक बादल घिर आए और मूसलाधार वर्षा होने लगी।' वाक्य में 'अचानक' किस प्रकार का क्रियाविशेषण है?
explanation: 'अचानक / एकाएक / सहसा' क्रिया के घटित होने की आकस्मिक रीति (ढंग) प्रकट करते हैं।

subject: Hindi Grammar
question: निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा शब्द 'अव्यय' (अविकारी) नहीं है?
options: सुंदर (विशेषण - विकारी शब्द है ; जैसे: सुंदर, सुंदरी, सुंदरों)
explanation: 'सुंदर' विशेषण (विकारी) है, जबकि 'और', 'धीरे-धीरे', 'किन्तु' अपरिवर्तनशील अव्यय हैं।

subject: Hindi Grammar
question:
कथन और कारण को ध्यानपूर्वक पढ़ें:
कथन (A): 'लड़का तेज दौड़ता है।' और 'लड़की तेज दौड़ती है।' दोनों वाक्यों में 'तेज' शब्द का रूप अपरिवर्तित रहता है।
कारण (R): 'तेज' एक रीतिवाचक क्रियाविशेषण (अव्यय) है, जिस पर कर्ता के लिंग (पुल्लिंग/स्त्रीलिंग) या वचन का कोई प्रभाव नहीं पड़ता।
सही विकल्प चुनें:
options: (A) और (R) दोनों सही हैं तथा (R), (A) की सही व्याख्या करता है।
(A) और (R) दोनों सही हैं, परन्तु (R), (A) की सही व्याख्या नहीं करता।
explanation: अव्यय शब्द लिंग, वचन, कारक से सर्वथा अप्रभावित और अपरिवर्तनीय (नित्य एकरूप) रहते हैं।

subject: Hindi Grammar
question:
Spot the IMPOSTER in the following classification of अव्यय भेदों में:
Group:
1. प्रतिदिन, अचानक - क्रियाविशेषण
2. के बिना, के पीछे - संबंधबोधक
3. और, किन्तु, क्योंकि - समुच्चयबोधक
4. पुस्तक, हिमालय - विस्मयादिबोधक
options: वर्ग 4 ('पुस्तक' और 'हिमालय' संज्ञा शब्द [विकारी] हैं, विस्मयादिबोधक अव्यय नहीं)
explanation: वर्ग 4 में 'पुस्तक' और 'हिमालय' संज्ञाएँ हैं, जबकि विस्मयादिबोधक 'अरे!', 'वाह!' आदि होते हैं।

subject: Hindi Grammar
question:
सुमेलित कीजिए (क्रियाविशेषण के 4 भेद और उनके प्रश्नवाचक पहचान शब्द):
(क) कालवाचक क्रियाविशेषण   -> (i) 'कब' (When)
(ख) स्थानवाचक क्रियाविशेषण -> (ii) 'कहाँ' (Where)
(ग) परिमाणवाचक क्रियाविशेषण-> (iii) 'कितना' (How much)
(घ) रीतिवाचक क्रियाविशेषण   -> (iv) 'कैसे / किस प्रकार' (How)
explanation: काल = कब; स्थान = कहाँ; परिमाण = कितना; रीति = कैसे।

subject: Hindi Grammar
question: समानाधिकरण समुच्चयबोधक के 4 उप-भेदों का सही मिलान कौन-सा है?
options: 1. संयोजक (और, तथा) ; 2. विभाजक (या, अथवा) ; 3. विरोधदर्शक (किन्तु, परन्तु, मगर) ; 4. परिणामदर्शक (इसलिए, अतः, फलस्वरूप)
विभाजक में हमेशा नकारात्मक क्रिया होती है
परिणामदर्शक केवल भविष्यत में आता है
explanation: समानाधिकरण के 4 रूप: संयोजक (जोड़ने वाला), विभाजक (विकल्प), विरोधदर्शक (अंतर), परिणामदर्शक (फलस्वरूप)।

subject: Hindi Grammar
question: निम्नलिखित वाक्यों में से किस वाक्य में 'निपात' का गलत स्थान पर प्रयोग होने से वाक्य का अभीष्ट अर्थ बदल गया है?
options: 'केवल उसने मुझे एक पुस्तक दी।' (अर्थ: सिर्फ उसी व्यक्ति ने दी, किसी और ने नहीं ; यदि 'उसने मुझे केवल एक पुस्तक दी' लिखा जाए तो अर्थ: सिर्फ एक ही पुस्तक दी)
explanation: निपात का स्थान बदलने से वाक्य में बल और अर्थ का केंद्र पूरी तरह बदल जाता है।

subject: Hindi Grammar
question: 'यद्यपि वह निर्धन है तथापि अत्यंत ईमानदार है।' वाक्य में 'यद्यपि...तथापि' किस प्रकार का समुच्चयबोधक युग्म है?
explanation: 'यद्यपि...तथापि' / 'यदि...तो' संकेतवाचक व्यधिकरण समुच्चयबोधक युग्म (Correlative conjunctions) हैं।

subject: Hindi Grammar
question: क्रियाविशेषण की रचना के आधार पर 'मूल क्रियाविशेषण' और 'यौगिक क्रियाविशेषण' में क्या अंतर होता है?
options: मूल क्रियाविशेषण बिना किसी प्रत्यय या रूपांतरण के स्वतंत्र रूप में आते हैं (जैसे: ठीक, अचानक, दूर, पास) ; जबकि यौगिक क्रियाविशेषण प्रत्यय, समास या द्विरुक्ति से बनते हैं (जैसे: प्रेमपूर्वक, हाथों-हाथ, धीरे-धीरे, प्रतिदिन)
दोनों में कोई अंतर नहीं होता
मूल क्रियाविशेषण केवल एक अक्षर का होता है
यौगिक क्रियाविशेषण केवल संस्कृत में होते हैं
explanation: मूल क्रियाविशेषण रूढ़ होते हैं; यौगिक क्रियाविशेषण प्रत्यय योग, समास अथवा शब्द-युग्मों की द्विरुक्ति से निर्मित होते हैं।

subject: Hindi Grammar
question: 'सावधान! आगे गहरा गड्ढा है।' वाक्य में 'सावधान!' किस प्रकार का विस्मयादिबोधक है?
explanation: 'सावधान! / होशियार! / बचो!' आने वाले खतरे के प्रति सतर्क करने वाले चेतावनीसूचक विस्मयादिबोधक अव्यय हैं।

subject: Hindi Grammar
question: निम्नलिखित में से किस वाक्य में 'स्थानवाचक क्रियाविशेषण' का शुद्ध प्रयोग हुआ है?
options: 'पक्षी आकाश में चारों ओर उड़ रहे हैं।' ('चारों ओर' क्रिया के घटित होने की दिशा/स्थान बता रहा है)
explanation: 'चारों ओर / इधर-उधर / सर्वत्र' स्थान व दिशा का बोध कराने वाले स्थानवाचक क्रियाविशेषण हैं।

subject: Hindi Grammar
question: 'हाय! बेचारा दुर्घटना में घायल हो गया।' वाक्य में 'हाय!' किस मनोभाव को व्यक्त करता है?
explanation: 'हाय! / उफ़! / आह!' दुःख, वेदना और शोक की तीव्र भावात्मक अभिव्यक्ति करते हैं।

subject: Hindi Grammar
question: प्रमुख 9 निपातों (ही, भी, तो, तक, मात्र, भर, केवल, सा, जी) का वाक्य में क्या सर्वोच्च प्रयोजन होता है?
options: ये किसी पद के साथ प्रयुक्त होकर उसके अर्थ को सीमित, निश्चित, विस्तारित या विशिष्ट भावात्मक बल (Emphatic force) प्रदान करते हैं
ये केवल वाक्य को लंबा बनाते हैं
ये संज्ञा का लिंग बदल देते हैं
ये क्रिया को भूतकाल में बदल देते हैं
explanation: निपात वाक्य में विशेष अर्थगत अवधारण, आग्रह, सीमा अथवा बल की सूक्ष्म अभिव्यक्ति हेतु प्रयुक्त होते हैं।

subject: Hindi Grammar
question: अव्यय (अविकारी शब्दों) का हिंदी भाषा संरचना में क्या केंद्रीय महत्व है?
options: अव्यय भाषा को सुगठित, प्रवाहपूर्ण और तार्किक बनाते हैं; ये उपवाक्यों को जोड़ते हैं, क्रिया की सटीक परिस्थितियाँ स्पष्ट करते हैं, और भाषा में सूक्ष्म मनोभावों तथा अर्थ-बल का संचार करते हैं
अव्यय केवल कविताओं में प्रयुक्त होते हैं
इनके बिना भी भाषा का रूप अपरिवर्तित रहता है
अव्यय का भाषा में कोई महत्व नहीं है
explanation: अव्यय भाषा की तार्किक सुसंबद्धता (Cohesion), मनोभाव प्रकटन और संश्लिष्ट वाक्य-संयोजन के अनिवार्य माध्यम हैं।
